    A closed chain makes chains unbounded #

    Going around a closed chain again and again gives chains of every length (ClosedChain.not_chainBounded), the converse of exists_closedChain.

            theorem LargeIndecomposable.RayCat.not_chainBounded_of_cyclic {Q : Type} [CategoryTheory.Category.{0, 0} Q] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms Q] [IsRayCategory Q] (m : ℕ) (f : ℕ → RayMor Q) (hne : ∀ (t : ℕ), (f t).snd.snd ≠ 0) (hP : ∀ i ≤ m, Peak (f (2 * i)) (f (2 * i + 1))) (hV : ∀ i < m, Valley (f (2 * i + 1)) (f (2 * i + 2))) (hV' : Valley (f (2 * m + 1)) (f 0)) :
            ¬ChainBounded Q

            A cyclic sequence with alternating peaks and valleys makes chains unbounded. The sequence f 0, …, f (2m+1) has peaks (f (2i), f (2i+1)) and valleys (f (2i+1), f (2i+2)), the last valley closing up with f 0.
